title: Periodical cicadas per acre: peak habitat vs. typical woodland

source.name: Periodical Cicada Information
source.publisher: University of Connecticut (Cicadas.uconn.edu, Cooley/Simon lab), density figures as reported in USDA Forest Service extension materials

notes: Entomologists estimate peak periodical cicada densities can reach up to about 1.5 million individuals per acre in prime habitat, versus roughly a few thousand per acre in an average wooded area -- part of why entomologists estimated the combined 2024 Brood XIX / Brood XIII emergence produced hundreds of billions, potentially over a trillion, cicadas across the two broods' combined range of roughly 16 states.
